sources.note: GITenberg clone checked: The-Iliad_2199, translator Samuel Butler. Prose, no line numbers: Stage B maps Greek line ranges to Butler's paragraphs.
Butler's Odyssey is #1727. The local clone The-Odyssey_3160 is Pope's verse translation (1725–26), not Butler: do not use 3160 for set readings (argus-the-dog memory is Pope; fine).

art.title: The Muses Urania and Calliope
art.why: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry, the 'goddess' the Iliad's first line asks to sing; the gallery's title names her (the description itself names no figures).

null: NGA has no Hector and Andromache. Girodet's 'Coriolanus Taking Leave of his Family' (1786, eedab1c0-c052-4a82-9c63-e03f95d1ca0e, unclaimed) shows a Roman hero's farewell, not Homer's; left for Hall IV.
null: no Achilles or Hector anywhere in the NGA paintings (searched titles and descriptions: achilles, hector, troy, trojan, iliad).
null: no Priam and Achilles at NGA.

art.title: Ulysses
art.why: Odysseus (Ulysses) himself, bearded, helmeted, hand to chest: the hero of the homecoming.

art.title: The Feast of the Gods
art.why: The Olympian gods carousing with satyrs: the session asks whether Homer's gods were any good. Subject is from Ovid, not Homer: say so. Spec wanted the underworld: none at NGA.

art.title: The Judgment of Paris
art.why: The spec's 'classical scene by Claude'; Paris's choice is where the Trojan war began. The description names no figures: the title does.

music.why: Spec: nothing Homeric; a grave, spacious opening.
Gentle requiem for the life Achilles gives up and the family Hector leaves.
Terror and pity at the death of Hector.
'Blessed are they that mourn': Priam and Achilles weeping together.
Tavener's Athene: Greek name, and a song of homecoming and rest.
A plea for mercy in a world the session finds short of it.
Spec choice; returns to the first session's music to close the frame.
